scope: Root causes and repairs for the Universe CI failures on develop, each bound to the run and job that produced it. Executed on the Primcast self-hosted fleet. No deployment, no production mutation, no GitHub-hosted runner.

causes.failingStep: No raw interface colour outside the allowlist
causes.firstCausalError: 3 raw interface colour literal(s) outside the allowlist: frontend/src/styles/_universe-portfolio-print.scss:14 #fff, :15 #111, :16 #444
causes.introducedBy: b893ca60 fix(portfolio): scope report print layout
causes.repair: The print sheet includes the universe-light-tokens mixin for the mounted report and takes background, colour and the soft foreground from those tokens. A printed page is paper, so it uses the measured light palette whatever theme the reader is viewing in, rather than introducing print-only literals no contrast test covers.
causes.verification: node scripts/universe/check-colors.mjs passes; sass compiles the partial to 6058 bytes; all 18 Documentation gates steps pass locally and the job succeeds on run 34016760588.

causes.failingStep: No obsolete upstream product marks / No third-party data origins
causes.firstCausalError: Two third-party blockchain data origins, and the upstream product's name, in the private submission accelerator directory and in its visual-QA fixtures. The literal strings are deliberately not quoted here so this record does not itself trip the gates it describes; they are the two accelerator status endpoints removed from private-submission.service.ts in this change.
causes.class: product runtime defect surfaced by a quality assertion
causes.introducedBy: 4886501c8 feat(intelligence): implement nine net-new explorer frontier products
causes.repair: The private submission reads no longer answer a failed request with an invented one. See the findings block below.
causes.verification: node scripts/universe/check-branding.mjs and check-origins.mjs pass; the backend suite asserts the unavailable behaviour, 8 assertions.

causes.repair: bitcoinjs-lib ~6.1.3 and tiny-secp256k1 2.2.4 are frontend dev dependencies, pinned to the versions the backend already resolves, and the spec imports them normally instead of reaching into a sibling package's install tree the job never creates. No assertion changed.
causes.verification: 28 of 28 assertions in swaps-package.spec.ts pass; the full frontend suite passes 1497 tests across 92 files; the Frontend build job reached the production build and every downstream gate on run 34016760588.

causes.failingStep: Repair a half-installed Rust toolchain before using it
causes.firstCausalError: cargo in use: none; line 30: cargo: command not found; exit code 127
causes.repair: The step reported 'no rustup on this runner' and then ran cargo anyway. It installs the pinned stable toolchain with a minimal profile when a runner has none, then proves it can read rust/gbt/Cargo.toml as before.
causes.verification: Backend build and test completed successfully on run 34016760588, runner universe-linux-super-167.

causes.firstCausalError: 8 errors: 2 unhandled promises and 6 awaits of non-@asyncSafe callees
causes.repair: NatsJetStreamEventBusProvider.connect and ClickHouseAnalyticalProvider.init both catch every path already, so they carry @asyncSafe and their void call sites are honest. The event bus listener wraps its delivery bookkeeping, because an emitter does not await a listener and a rejection there would surface as an unhandled rejection. The six awaits are of callees that reject deliberately and whose route handler turns the rejection into an answer, so the awaiting contexts carry @asyncUnsafe, the annotation this repository already uses in 57 places.
causes.verification: eslint reports 0 errors; backend unit suite passes 683 tests across 73 suites; the job succeeds on run 34016760588.

causes.failingStep: Every window a phone can be, on WebKit
causes.firstCausalError: browserType.launch: Host system is missing dependencies to run browsers: libicu74, libxml2, libvpx9
causes.measuredHostState: 31.14.40.195 runs Ubuntu 26.04 (resolute) and provides libicu78, libxml2-16 and libvpx12. libicu74, libxml2 and libvpx9 have no installation candidate on that release, so no apt install on the host satisfies the sonames Playwright's WebKit build links. The runner service account is github-runner and is in the docker group; Docker Engine 29.7.2 is active.
causes.repair: The job stays on the fleet and runs inside mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.49.0-noble, pinned to the Playwright version in scripts/universe/visual-qa/package.json, which carries both engines and every library they link. This is the fleet running a matched container, not an escape to a GitHub-hosted runner.
causes.verification: On run 34016760588 the container initialised, the production build, harness install, engine fetch and gateway all succeeded, and WebKit launched and ran for seven minutes, which it could not previously do at all.

causes.firstCausalError: AssertionError: the mining navigation item exists (actual 0, expected true) at parity-regressions.test.mjs:26
causes.repair: The gate matched the element on the exact class string 'nav-item mining'. The element carries mobile-primary as well, so the match returned nothing and the gate read as the item being absent rather than as it being ungated. It matches on id="btn-pools" now, the way the charts case beside it already did. All three assertions on the element are unchanged and the element satisfies them: the item is shown when activeChain is not bitcoin, and it routes through chainRoute('mining').

causes.failingStep: Every window a phone can be, on WebKit
causes.firstCausalError: browserContext.newPage: Target page, context or browser has been closed, after seven minutes of running checks
causes.repair: A container gets 64 MB of /dev/shm by default, which is where WebKit puts its shared buffers, and it does not degrade when that runs out. The container asks for --shm-size=2gb --ipc=host.

causes.job: Frontend build, Mobile and adaptive layout, WebKit and Firefox
causes.failingStep: Every route renders and finishes, at a phone and a desktop width; Every window a phone can be
causes.firstCausalError: The step was still running at the job cap with no output written.
causes.measurement: The shared route list in scripts/universe/visual-qa/capture.mjs held 32 entries at the last green run 0f3e5a19 and holds 244 now. The broad pass measured 5m50s at 32 routes; the same work at 244 does not fit a 45 minute job. mobile-check.mjs walks the same list, so the Chromium mobile job and the WebKit job carry the same growth.
causes.repair: capture.mjs and mobile-check.mjs take --shard=i/n, slicing by position so every route lands in exactly one shard. The three steps run three shards at once against the one gateway, each with its own output and log, and the step fails if any shard fails. The Playwright container asks for four gigabytes of shared memory because three engines now run at once.
causes.verification: The partition was checked directly: 244 routes split 82, 81, 81, with every id present exactly once. All ten visual QA unit tests pass.

causes.failingStep: A third engine, on the checks that do not need a thumb
causes.firstCausalError: Running Nightly as root in a regular user's session is not supported. ($HOME is /github/home which is owned by uid 999.)
causes.repair: The step sets HOME=/root, which is the fix Playwright itself names. It appeared only once the job moved into a container, and only on Firefox; WebKit passed all three shards in the same job.
causes.verification: Pending the run on the head that carries it.

causes.failingStep: Every route renders and finishes, at a phone and a desktop width
causes.class: product defect and a fixture gap, surfaced by making the gate finish
causes.firstCausalError: 2 unmatched fixture requests on bootstrap-planner; 3 pages that never finished, on mining at both widths and tx at 1440; .chain-toggle absent on the chain-menu scenario at both widths.
causes.measurement: mining and chain-menu were in the 32 route list that passed at the last green run 0f3e5a19. tx and bootstrap-planner were added after it and had never been measured. The broad pass has not completed since, so none of this had been reported.
causes.repair: The bootstrap wiring is repaired: the frontend was posting to /bootstrap/snapshots/verify and /bootstrap/planner, and the backend mounts neither. It now calls /bootstrap/verifications and /bootstrap/plans, and the backend gains the /bootstrap/chainstates list route the chainstates page was already calling and receiving a 404 for. That mismatch is why the AssumeUTXO verifier had an error branch at all, and why that branch reported the snapshot as valid. The fixture keys follow the real routes.
causes.remaining: mining, tx and chain-menu are re-run serially to separate a real regression from the timing of three browsers sharing a runner. The broad pass is serial again and the frontend job carries a 90 minute budget for it; the WebKit job keeps its three shards, which passed.

causes.failingStep: A third engine, on the checks that do not need a thumb
causes.class: product defect on newly reachable coverage
causes.note: Firefox had not run in this job at all: before the container it could not find its system libraries, and inside the container it could not start as root with a foreign HOME. These are its first results here, not regressions.
findings: home@phone-320: the replacement fee cell holds a number and its unit on one line, and together they extend five pixels past the cell with no way to reach them. Chromium rounds the same layout away; Firefox measures it. Repaired: the unit wraps to a second line at 360px and below, so the number is never the part that is clipped.

home@tablet-768: page.goto exceeded 45000ms waiting for domcontentloaded, at one viewport out of seven for the same route in the same run. Not yet explained. Left unchanged and measured again rather than absorbed into a longer timeout.

causes.failingStep: Every route renders and finishes, at a phone and a desktop width
causes.class: contract mismatch and fixture coverage gap
causes.result: unfinished pages fell to zero. The mining, tx and chain-menu findings from the previous run were real and are fixed. What remained was 96 pages whose API requests had no fixture and failed closed.
causes.finding: 43 distinct endpoints had no fixture. 40 are mounted by the explorer backend and 2 by the overlay; they simply had no fixture. One was a path mismatch: the whole mining-decentralized frontend service calls /api/v1/intelligence/mining-decentralized/*, and the backend mounts /api/v1/intelligence/mining/decentralized/*. All five of its calls 404 in production. The frontend now calls the mounted path and the fixture keys follow.
causes.method: Each fixture body is the response the service that serves the route actually returns, obtained by importing the compiled service and calling the method its handler calls. The two overlay reads are the deployment's own answers, read from it. Writing a body from the route name is how a page passes here and 404s in production, which is what the bootstrap and mining routes were already doing.
causes.verification: 43 fixtures added, 206 keys total, fixture contract test passes, both packages typecheck.

causes.failingStep: A third engine, on the checks that do not need a thumb
causes.class: harness flake, not a product defect
causes.evidence: One navigation timeout per run, at a different route and window each time: home at tablet-768, then tx in landscape. Same 45 second budget, same commit range, and every other window for those routes passed in the same run. WebKit passed all three of its shards in both runs.
causes.repair: The navigation takes one retry at the same budget before it is called a failure. A page that genuinely never loads still fails, because it fails twice. The budget itself is unchanged, so a real slow page is still reported.

causes.failingStep: Every window a phone can be, measured with a thumb
causes.class: product defect on newly reachable coverage
causes.note: This job is gated on the frontend job, which has failed since 3 September, so it had not run to completion since the frontier products shipped. 226 findings across three shards, all on those pages, none of them created by this branch.

findings.undeclared scroll regions: About 200. Bootstrap gives .table-responsive overflow-x: auto and no tabindex or role, so a clipped row has no keyboard route and is not announced. 102 of them across 89 files, none declared. Each now carries tabindex=0, which is what Bootstrap documents for a responsive table.
findings.content clipped by the page shell: Sixteen pages lost between 7px and 330px at 320px. The product header is a flex row that does not wrap, and the monospace reference under the title has no spaces to break on, while .page-shell carries overflow: clip so the excess is cut rather than scrolled. A narrow-width partial wraps that row and its button group and lets an opaque identifier break anywhere.
findings.touch targets: Two pages put three 24px checkboxes in a row. They take the 44px token at compact widths, which is the smaller of the two platform floors.

causes.verification: frontend typecheck clean, lint 0 errors, 1497 tests pass, colour, palette, fill and text gates pass.

secondPass.note: The scroll region, header wrap and checkbox fixes took the gate from 226 findings to 22. One of the 22 was caused by the first fix: overflow-wrap: anywhere changes an element min-content width, so inside a table cell it collapsed a monospace link to one character per line, 24px wide and 607px tall. That is break-word now, which breaks the same strings without shrinking the box.
alsoRepaired: A flex child is min-width auto by default and will not shrink however its content wraps. That was the other half of the header overflow, and it is why the staking delegation heading still reached past the edge after the first pass.
Three pre blocks scroll sideways and now declare it, the same fault the tables had.
A select sized by its longest option, and a badge holding a long state word, both take the width of the phone rather than pushing the row out.
The checkbox floor now applies in landscape as well, which the gate measures separately.
The docs page ends inside .doc-content, its own scrolling region, so the shell bottom reservation never reached the last section and the final heading sat under the bar.

findings.severity: counterfeit success on a user-facing operation
findings.was: PrivateSubmissionApiService answered every failed request with an invented response through catchError(() => of(...)). A private broadcast that never reached a relay returned a submission token and status 'relayed_to_pools'. A receipt verification returned verified: true and signature_valid: true. The accelerator directory returned two third-party providers. The transaction and block ordering pages substituted a fixed txid and block hash when the address named none.
findings.backendWas: The service returned constants for every read. verifyAcceleratorReceipt returned verified: true whenever four fields were non-empty, with no signature check of any kind. submitPrivate recorded a token in a Map that nothing relayed.
findings.now: Frontend reads return what the API returned or they error. The backend raises a typed SubmissionEvidenceError naming the integration it waits on: unavailable-relay, unavailable-registry or unavailable-source. The routes map that to 503 with the stage and the message. Each surface renders the failure. Receipt validation keeps its one real check, the structural one, reports a malformed receipt as 400 with its faults named, and reports a structurally complete receipt as unverified with stage unavailable-registry while there is no provider key to verify it against.

findings.severity: same class, not repaired in this change
findings.observation: The catchError fallback pattern appears across frontend/src/app/universe. Counted by what each one actually returns, rather than by how many files contain the call, because they are not the same defect: 26 return null, 16 return an empty collection, 2 return an explicit failure state, and the rest returned a populated record no source produced. Only the last class invents an answer, and none of those remain.

returns-null.verdict: honest. An optional read that is absent reads as absent.

returns-empty-collection.verdict: weak. An empty list states that there is nothing, when the truth is that the service could not be asked. Not repaired here, and not a fabricated record.

returns-explicit-failure-state.verdict: honest. The consumer renders it as a failure.

returns-invented-record.verdict: repaired. Was 21 across three services plus the surfaces in FIND-PRIVSUB-01, FIND-FALSEPASS-01 and FIND-FALSEPASS-02.

findings.note: An earlier revision of this record listed nineteen files by name and called them all the same finding. That overstated it: most of those files return null or an empty collection. The classification above is measured rather than counted by grep.

findings.severity: a cryptographic check reported as passed when it never ran
findings.observation: Four surfaces reported a verification result that no check produced. Each one is the whole of what its page offers, so a reader had no way to tell a checked artifact from an unchecked one.

repaired.was: The error handler set the report to valid, with a status of pinned_core_verified and a block hash, so a failed request rendered as "Snapshot Commitments Verified Authentic. Safe to load."
repaired.now: A failed request reports the failure and shows no verdict.

repaired.was: The error handler set the report to valid, with an aggregate public key and a cosigner count, so a failed request rendered as "MuSig2 Key Aggregation Valid".
repaired.now: A failed request reports the failure and shows no verdict. The duplicate-cosigner check, which is real and local, is unchanged.

repaired.was: No request and no engine. After a 450 ms timer any input at all produced valid, with an invented schema id, contract id, genesis txid, transition count, seal count, and the sentence "All single-use seals and transition DAG hashes match Bitcoin commitments." The page badged it "Bitcoin confirmed" and "All Outpoints Closed".
repaired.now: The validator reports that this deployment carries no RGB validation engine, and that nothing was uploaded.

repaired.was: verifyProof$ answered a failed request with valid, a Bitcoin block height, a block hash and an attestation type. upgradeProof$ answered with upgraded and an invented proof. stampDigest$ answered with a proof string whose own bytes read mock. The overview, calendars and anchors reads answered with invented records.
repaired.now: Every call returns what the API returned or errors. The five components render the failure.

repaired.was: Two invented Git attestations, each badged "VERIFIED IN BITCOIN", one attributed to a named person, with no request behind them.
repaired.now: The page says it has no attestation source and that nothing here has been checked against Bitcoin.

repaired.was: A fixed four-step operation stack ending in "Block 864201 Merkle Root Validated", rendered whatever the reader pasted, with no decoder in the page.
repaired.now: The page says it has no proof decoder and that nothing here has been decoded.

stillCarryingThePattern.note: Repaired in the same change. See FIND-FALSEPASS-02.

findings.observation: The three services that answered a failed request with verified: true, and the BOLT12 decoder that read nothing, are repaired on the same terms as the rest.

repaired.change: Seven invented fallbacks removed, including the public package verification that reported itself verified. Five components render the failure.
Six invented fallbacks removed, including two that reported a conformance case as verified. Four components render the failure, and the case replay reports its own.
Nine invented fallbacks removed, including the Guix artifact verification that reported itself verified. Eight components render the failure.

repaired.was: decode() echoed the input back with an invented description, an invented blinded-route count and a badge reading "Valid BOLT12 Syntax", for any string at all. No decoder exists in the page.
repaired.now: It reports that this deployment carries no BOLT12 decoder and shows no summary.

findings.alsoFixed: Four detail routes substituted a fixed id when the address named none, so each reported on the same record whatever opened it: a round, a conformance case, an advisory and a node. Each now says the address names nothing.

stillCarryingTheLowerSeverityVariant.note: Two reads in lightning-standards degrade to an empty list rather than to invented records. An empty list still states that there is nothing, when the truth is that the service could not be asked, but it does not manufacture a record. The sixteen files in FIND-FALLBACK-01 that are not verification surfaces are also unchanged.

localVerification.visualQaSourceGates: progress-gate, chain-page-audit, address-page-audit and parity-regressions all pass

notVerifiedHere: Migrations and repositories against a real database, which needs the CI database service.
The visual matrix and mobile shards, which are gated on the frontend job and run on the fleet.
Universe production smoke, which is a live-origin check against production and is out of scope for a no-deployment task.

requiredChecks.legacyWorkflowOwnership: The legacy .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers only on master, and none of the five required contexts on develop belongs to it. It owns no required coverage here, so nothing was retargeted and no build matrix was duplicated.
requiredChecks.noDeploymentOnMerge: Merging to develop starts no deployment. universe-release-artifact.yml is workflow_dispatch only, universe-production-smoke.yml is dispatch or schedule against a live origin, docker.yml builds on version tags or master pull requests, and the legacy ci.yml is master only.
